summary: Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2001) under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under G. Raj. She held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend A. van Nooten is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2007).

Barend Faddegon was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University (PhD -1906) under Speyer, Kern, and Uhlenbeck. He taught at Amsterdam (1908–1944) and visited Harvard University (1926–1927).

Barend J. ter Haar specializes in sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied under Susan Naquin and Erik Zürcher at Leiden University (PhD ~1984–1990). His posts include KNAW (~1990–1994), Heidelberg (~1994–2000), Leiden (~2000–2013), and Hamburg (~2018).

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University (PhD ~1967–1972). He held posts at ANU, the University of Munich, Leiden University, and the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

Barry Kerzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC (MD ~1972–1976), and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He taught medicine at the University of Washington (1985–1989) and later held posts at CIHTS and HKU.

Barry Tse works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Federation University, Queensland, Liverpool, and James Cook University Singapore (PhD 2021–2025). He held teaching posts at JCU Singapore (2022–2026) and the University of Newcastle (2026).

Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Liaoning University and at Ghent University (PhD 1990–1994) under Charles Willemen. He was appointed Associate Professor at Ghent University in 1990.
Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian who studied at Kiel University (~1794–1796). He held chairs at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1813) and the University of Bonn (~1823–1831).
Basil Gould was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He was educated at New College, Oxford (~1902–1906) and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1907.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. ~1852–1853) under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He held professorships at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Batakrishna Ghosh was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Hanns Oertel (~1931–1935). He later worked as a librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and edited the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (-1905), he taught there (1908–1917) and held positions at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences, Buryat State Pedagogical Institute, and IOS RAS.

Beata Grant is a sinologist working in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Stanford University (~1980–1987), held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley (~1987–1989), and became Associate Professor at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989).

Beatrice Erskine Lane was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College (~1894–1898) under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, and at Columbia University (~1906–1908). She was appointed professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer was an Indologist who studied at Maryland and Heidelberg (Magister 1968–1971). She taught at Maryland (1971–1975), Heidelberg (1973–1976), the University of Hamburg (1982), European University Viadrina, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1989–1991).
Bedika Rai is an academic active in Buddhist studies. She served as an Assistant Professor at Salesian College (2010–2019) and at Kalipada Ghosh Tarai Mahavidyalaya starting in 2019.

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna (PhD 1897–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1905) and as Professor at Charles University (1919).
Bedřich Votýpka was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Josef Zubatý at Charles University (1885–1892). He later served as a gymnasium professor at Gymnázium Benešov.

Beier Wang specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Wang studied at the University of Toronto, the University of Hong Kong, and the University of Leipzig (PhD 2021), where Wang served as a Research Assistant (2022–2025).
